page: Microsoft Azure M64s is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8280M processor running at 2.7 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 105 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX-512 instructions. It is equipped with 1024 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 16 GB per core. Additionally, the instance includes 2097 GB of local SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng, Geekbench, and single-threaded compression tests scoring in the bottom 10%. However, multi-core capabilities are more robust, with multi-core stress-ng, Geekbench, and Passmark CPU scores landing in the middle 50%. Notably, memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is strong, reaching 215.58 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25%. Database operations and Redis SET performance remain in the average tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the M64s offers high resource density, particularly in memory capacity and local SSD storage, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads despite its modest single-core CPU speeds. The trade-off lies in its lower single-threaded efficiency. This server is best suited for large-scale databases, memory-intensive enterprise applications, data caching layers, and multi-threaded analytical workloads that require massive RAM footprints rather than high single-core clock speeds.
